messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a quick, step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and at a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a good wipe‑down, replace strings if needed, and tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows buyers you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, and local classifieds. Look at similar models, ages, and conditions. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively without underselling. | | **3. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the body, neck, headstock, fretboard, and any imperfections from multiple angles. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Great photos attract more views and reduce back‑and‑forth about condition. | | **4. Write a Clear Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, condition notes, any upgrades, and why you’re selling. | Transparency builds trust and reduces negotiations over hidden issues. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for gear, offers buyer protection.
• **eBay** – broad audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local Music Stores** – may buy outright or offer consignment. | Different platforms reach different audiences; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Set a Realistic Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point keeps you from selling too low. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Shipping** – use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and insured freight.
• **Pickup** – safer for high‑value items, saves shipping costs. | Shipping adds cost and risk; pickup is simpler but limits your audience. | | **8. Secure Payment** | • For local sales: cash or Venmo/PayPal “Friends & Family” (no fees).
• For online: PayPal Goods & Services, or a platform‑provided escrow. | Protect yourself against fraud and ensure you receive payment before handing over the guitar. | | **9. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | Keep communication polite, stick to your minimum acceptable price, and be ready to walk away if terms aren’t met. | Good manners and firm boundaries lead to smoother deals. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Sign a simple bill of sale (many sites provide templates). Transfer ownership details if required. | Provides legal proof of transfer and protects both parties. | ### Quick Tips - **Timing:** Listings posted mid‑week tend to get more views than weekend posts. - **Safety:** Meet in public places for local pickups; bring a friend if possible. - **Extras:** Offer a small bundle (e.g., a capo or strap) if you’re willing—it can sweeten the deal. - **Feedback:** Ask buyers to leave a review on the platform; positive feedback boosts future sales. Good luck! If you need help estimating the value or setting up a listing on a specific site, let me know.
